rulings.challenge_claim: The rejected_alternative's premise that no root repeats across the gap to 23:24-25 is byte-false: the father root recurs in 23:22, 23:24, and 23:25.
rulings.grounds: UPHELD as a real defect: byte tier (verse_map_oshb.json direct splice, re-collated GREEN/byte via collate.py --json). The father root opens לְ֭אָבִיךָ (23:22), recurs as the construct אֲבִ֣י (23:24), and again as אָבִ֥יךָ (23:25, near-identical wordform to 23:22's token apart from the proclitic/cantillation); the mother token אִמֶּֽךָ (23:22) recurs as וְאִמֶּ֑ךָ (23:25). Three verses, not zero, carry the root -- the row's own word 'root' is refuted directly, not merely a cognate-level stretch. This does NOT flip the boundary call: 23:23 (buying truth) remains a topically distinct verse independently sufficient to interrupt continuity, so the standalone P10-017 unit still holds -- both primaries and I agree on that point. REFINE on severity: LF called this low; I rule medium, matching OL's call, because an explicit 'root' claim is falsified by exact recurring wordforms (not a same-root-different-word cognate as in P10-018), and per TOOLKIT's cross-seam-cohesion rule a byte-true device straddling a row's own seam must be DISCLOSED, not denied, even when it is not a driver.
rulings.remedy: Rewrite the rejected_alternative sentence to disclose the recurrence by name and digit (father/mother root recurs in 23:22, 23:24, and 23:25 -- 3 verses) as texture, while keeping 23:23's distinct commerce topic as the actual, independently sufficient ground for the standalone call. Test: check_refs_mirror.py (verse mentioned in prose now correctly cross-referenced) plus a manual byte re-check confirming the recurrence is named with a digit rather than denied -- the test that killed the original claim.

rulings.challenge_claim: 23:29 carries an undisclosed ketiv/qere note sitting inside the verse quoted as the row's central 'six-fold' rhetorical evidence, and the verse-31 form the row calls 'the span's one plain imperative' is grammatically a negated prohibitive, not a true imperative.
rulings.grounds: TWO items bundled in one challenge -- adjudicated separately. (1) The K/Q-disclosure sub-claim is the SAME defect as LF's P10-021 item (same verse, same inventory count, same hazard class); see the LF entry above for the full byte/policy grounding -- confirmed, high severity. (2) The morphology sub-claim is DISTINCT and not raised by LF: אַל תֵּ֥רֶא (23:31) is the negative particle plus a 2ms prefix-conjugation form of the root r-'-h ('see') -- a standard prohibitive/vetitive construction. Biblical Hebrew's morphological imperative is never negated with the particle 'al -- negative commands are formed with 'al plus a prefix-conjugation (jussive-shaped) verb, which is exactly the pattern here -- so labeling this 'the span's one plain imperative' misidentifies the form. This is corroborated even at the WEB layer: verse_map_web.json renders Prov.23.31 as "Don't look at the wine" (web:Prov.23.31) -- a negative-command gloss that already sits uneasily under the row's own 'plain imperative' label. Per TOOLKIT.md, morphological form claims (imperative/jussive/participle) are not machine-checkable with the staged extract, so this is argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings, per OL's own disclosed method -- correctly argued, and upheld. This mislabeling does not overturn the wisdom_poem call: the poem's other structural markers (riddle-opening at 23:29, extended aftermath, closing quoted speech at 23:35) remain valid and sufficient on their own. OL's overall severity call of high for the combined challenge is upheld: the K/Q sub-claim alone clears the high bar, and the morphology sub-claim is an independent, real accuracy defect in the same row's structural argument.
rulings.remedy: (1) Same K/Q disclosure cure as the LF item. (2) Replace 'the span's one plain imperative' with an accurate label (e.g. 'the span's one negative command' or 'prohibitive') in both the rationale and device_notes; the poem-shape argument does not depend on the form being a true imperative and loses nothing by the correction. Test: no machine check exists for morphology (a standing TOOLKIT gap) -- the re-verification standard is a manual pointed-bytes-plus-both-witnesses check, matching the method OL used here; flag 'imperative' labels elsewhere in Prov admonition_unit / wisdom_poem rows for the same manual check if the writer brief's controlled vocabulary continues to invite the label.
